-   **Rarity note:** Uncommon/Rare species in Florida, found in areas where seagrapes are found.

## Natural history notes

A tiny tortricid moth characterized by narrow grayish-brown to tan forewings with subtle darker mottling and folded resting posture typical of seedworm moths. In Florida, it has been recorded from seagrape, especially in coastal or tropical hardwood habitats where seagrape grows. Adults are small, mostly nocturnal, and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed within seeds, fruits, or related plant structures, helping move seagrape plant material into the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
